---
title: "Quasi-stars under infall"
subtitle: "A steady envelope model, a Julia TITAN, and what they show"
toc: false
---

Santarelli, Bellinger and collaborators model the "Little Red Dots" seen by JWST as late-stage
quasi-stars: a black hole of about $10^5\,M_\odot$ inside a $10^6\,M_\odot$ envelope that radiates at the
Eddington limit with a surface near 6000 K [@santarelli2026lrd; @santarelli2026quest]. This book records what we
found when we tested two of their working assumptions and how we built the tools to do it.

1. **Is the photosphere in LTE?** Simple rate estimates say that hydrogen there is controlled by radiative,
   not collisional, rates (@sec-lte).
2. **Does a ~6000 K hydrostatic photosphere survive the infall that feeds the black hole?** A steady model with a
   free-fall accretion shock as its outer boundary finds two branches of solutions and a fold beyond which no
   steady star exists (@sec-branches).
3. **What does the dynamics do?** We ported the radiation-hydrodynamics code TITAN [@gehmeyr1994] from
   Fortran to Julia, verified it against the original, and added the quasi-star physics. After four numerical
   defects were fixed, it follows the envelope stably while the accretion rate rises a thousandfold to
   $3\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$. At that rate the answer depends on resolving a thin, hot cooling layer behind the
   accretion shock, which only the adaptive grid does (@sec-titan-port, @sec-titan-qs).

::: {.callout-note title="How to read the status of a statement"}
Every result carries one of four labels.
**[computed]** is an output of the code described here, reproducible from the repository.
**[tested]** is a computed result pinned by an automated test (a ✓ badge links to the test).
**[estimate]** is an order-of-magnitude rate or budget with textbook approximations.
**[interpretation]** is our reading of the results, not separately derived.
Open problems are said to be open.
:::

The equations of the steady model are evaluated in the browser by a tested Rust core compiled to WebAssembly.
A superscript ⟨name⟩ links to the function that evaluates an equation, a ✓ badge links to the test that pins a
number, and a *lab* button opens the laboratory in the state that reproduces an experiment. The TITAN figures
replay simulation output produced by the Julia code in the same repository; @sec-experiments lists every
experiment with the command that reproduces it.
